title: Derived tensor equation from the ordinary coefficient square
statement: For commutative condensed rings R,S and a ring-object map a with exact internal scalar extension on every scheme, let f:X to Y be a scheme morphism. Suppose the ordinary pullIso(a,f).symm is monoidal for the specified internalScalarMonoidal and monoidal_upperStar structures. Then the derived scalar comparison mu, actual geometric tensor maps d, and canonical localized coefficient path theta satisfy P_S(mu_Y) followed by d_S followed by tensor(theta_A,theta_B) = theta_(A tensor B) followed by T_X(d_R) followed by mu_X, for every A,B in the unbounded derived category of internal R_Y-modules [def-sfb-coefficient-scalar-tensor-realization-data]. This states only the derived tensor equation, not section scalar realization or ordinary square monoidality.

proof.text: Install the specified internalScalarMonoidal and monoidal_upperStar structures. Apply the adopted source theorem Functor.map_leftDerivedTensorComparison_comp_eq_of_iso with F1 = upperStar R f, F2 = extendScalars a_X, G1 = extendScalars a_Y, G2 = upperStar S f, and tau = (pullIso a f).symm. The proved private wrapper canonical_tensor_square stores this equation in the proposition TensorSquare before specializing at objects, so matching the existing monoidal data does not unfold their concrete tensor constructions. The hypothesis supplies exactly the ordinary monoidality assumption; all four functors are additive exact left adjoints preserving flat objects.

Identify the path comparison with coefficientScalarPathIso by the defining equality of isomorphisms. Identify each scalar comparison with internalScalarTensorComparison by the defining equality of natural transformations, then evaluate at the two objects. Identify each geometric comparison using leftDerivedUpperStarTensor_eq_leftDerivedTensorComparison, again evaluated at the two objects. Give the canonical comparison aliases their original bifunctor types and evaluate the stored TensorSquare equation. Expand tensorHom into its two whiskered factors. The proved private categorical helper tensor_square_from_inv transports the component equalities into the composite equation, precomposes with the hom component of the path isomorphism at A tensor B, cancels its inverse, and reverses the equation. This gives exactly the required displayed equation.

theorem coefficientScalarDerivedTensorSquare {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hmono : letI := internalScalarMonoidal a X
      letI := internalScalarMonoidal a Y
      letI := monoidal_upperStar R f
      letI := monoidal_upperStar S f
      NatTrans.IsMonoidal (pullIso a f).symm.hom) :
    ∀ A B : DerivedCategory (ModuleRingedComparison.internalModules R Y),
      (moduleObjectDerivedPullback S f).map
          (((internalScalarTensorComparison a Y).app A).app B) ≫
        coefficientGeometricTensorComparison S f
          ((internalScalarExtension a Y).obj A)
          ((internalScalarExtension a Y).obj B) ≫
        ((derivedTensor S X).map ((coefficientScalarPathIso a f).hom.app A)).app
          ((moduleObjectDerivedPullback S f).obj
            ((internalScalarExtension a Y).obj B)) ≫
        ((derivedTensor S X).obj
          ((internalScalarExtension a X).obj
            ((moduleObjectDerivedPullback R f).obj A))).map
              ((coefficientScalarPathIso a f).hom.app B) =
      (coefficientScalarPathIso a f).hom.app (((derivedTensor R Y).obj A).obj B) ≫
        (internalScalarExtension a X).map
          (coefficientGeometricTensorComparison R f A B) ≫
        ((internalScalarTensorComparison a X).app
          ((moduleObjectDerivedPullback R f).obj A)).app
            ((moduleObjectDerivedPullback R f).obj B)
